Sample hourly rate build-up

Builds a made-up hourly rate from a base rate, add-on percentages and a fee, one step at a time. Every rule and number in it is invented to exercise the calculator template.

What this tool does not cover

  • Every rule, rate and threshold here is fictional. Do not use the result for a real proposal, invoice or contract.
  • It covers one labour category at a time and does not add travel, materials or other direct costs.
  • It does not check whether a rate is allowable under any real regulation.

Your values

The rate paid for one hour of work, before anything is added. From 0.00 to 500.00, with up to 2 decimal places.

From 0 to 10000, with up to 1 decimal place.

Choose one. The values are listed under “Fee tiers” below.

How the result is worked out

StepWhat it isHow it is worked outResultSource
1 Fringe (per hour) Base hourly rate × Fringe percentage ÷ 100, rounded to 2 decimal places. - [1]
2 Rate with fringe (per hour) Base hourly rate + Fringe, rounded to 2 decimal places. - [2]
3 Overhead (per hour) Rate with fringe × Overhead percentage ÷ 100, rounded to 2 decimal places. - [2]
4 Cost rate (per hour) Base hourly rate + Fringe + Overhead, rounded to 2 decimal places. -
5 Fee before the cap (per hour) Cost rate × Fee tier ÷ 100, rounded to 2 decimal places. - [3]
6 Fee (per hour) The smallest of: Fee before the cap; Largest fee allowed, rounded to 2 decimal places. - [3]
7 Loaded rate (per hour) Cost rate + Fee, rounded to 2 decimal places. -
8 Loaded rate above the minimum (per hour) Loaded rate − Minimum billable rate, rounded to 2 decimal places. - [4]
9 Billable rate (per hour) The largest of: Loaded rate; Minimum billable rate, rounded to 2 decimal places. - [4]
10 Total for the hours Billable rate × Hours of work, rounded to 2 decimal places. -
11 Working days (days) Hours of work ÷ Hours in a working day, rounded to 1 decimal place. -

Every step uses exact decimal arithmetic. Where a step is rounded, a half is rounded away from zero: 0.125 to 2 decimal places is 0.13.
